bullets.title: Mag7/NDX vs. Breadth: Rotation in Full Swing, Not a Market Top
bullets.body: Mag7 shed >$1T in market cap in the week, down ~7% MTD (NVDA -8.6%, GOOGL -8.3%) while the equal-weight S&P and IWM outperformed—S&P A/D line positive 11 of 12 sessions and Russell 2000 up ~21% YTD, biggest small-cap outperformance since 2003. Multiple desks frame this as crowded-momentum unwind driven by leveraged ETF cascade ($42bn forced supply mid-week) and positioning cleanup, not a fundamental break in the AI capex cycle. JPM, Piper, and Barclays/Stifel all raised SPX year-end PTs to 7,800 on ~10% consensus EPS upgrades.

bullets.title: Fed Pivots Hawkish: Rate-Hike Risk By Year-End Now Base Case for Several Desks
bullets.body: Core PCE printed 0.32% MoM in May—core services ex-housing running 4%+ annualized and above 6% on 3-month pace. Fed speakers Goolsbee and Kashkari flagged 'disturbing' services inflation; new Chair Warsh signaled meeting-by-meeting hawkishness with reduced forward guidance. BofA now expects 75bp of hikes, Deutsche Bank 50bp, and JPM frames a 1999-2000 mid-cycle analog implying 50-100bp tightening. Market pricing shifted to ~40-50bp of hikes by year-end from near-zero prior. The critical threshold is whether core PCE averages ≤0.21% MoM; prints above that range over 2-3 months would force hike pricing.

bullets.title: AI Capex Supercycle Intact: $5.5T Through 2030, But Margin/Concentration Risk Rising
bullets.body: Five hyperscalers (GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, META, ORCL) tracking ~$730B capex in 2026 (+77% YoY); JPM raised its AI capex estimate to $5.5T through 2030. AI infrastructure expected to contribute ~60% of S&P 500 EPS growth in Q2 with MU+NVDA alone accounting for >40%. However, Goldman flags momentum crowding at 99th percentile in AI infrastructure and warns of flash-crash risk in Low Quality/Speculative Growth segments given levered ETF exposure of -$16bn/1% move.

bullets.title: Memory Supercycle: MU Blowout, 16 Strategic Customer Agreements, Tight Supply Through 2028
bullets.body: Micron F3Q revenue of $41.46B (+15% vs consensus) with 84.9% gross margin, guided Q4 to $50B and 86% GM—both ~15-20% above consensus. MU disclosed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements covering ~20% DRAM and ~33% NAND volume on 5-year take-or-pay terms with $100B+ minimum revenue and $22B in customer deposits; floor pricing 'well above prior peak margins.' Management sees supply-demand tightness persisting beyond CY27 with no line of sight on equilibration. Multiple desks raised PTs to $1,100-$1,675; HBM TAM now expected to cross $100B in 2027, one year earlier than prior.

bullets.title: Tech Price Inflation: AAPL/MSFT Hiking Hardware Prices on 400%+ DRAM Cost Surge
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac and iPad prices 15-25% (first such move of this magnitude) citing data center-driven DRAM/NAND cost surge; MSFT raised Xbox prices for the third time in 13 months (+$100-$150 Aug 1). Core PCE gets a 0.54pp boost from tech price inflation while CPI sees only 0.1pp due to shelter weighting differences. PSC Macro estimates tech prices will add a lasting inflation tax; Core PCE is now not expected to reach 2% until 1H 2027 rather than 2026.

bullets.title: Korea Chipmaker Selloff: Leveraged ETF Cascade Triggered 10% KOSPI Drop
bullets.body: South Korea's KOSPI fell ~10% on June 23 (5th largest single-day drop in history) as leveraged single-stock chip ETFs hit circuit breakers; SK Hynix and Samsung each fell >12%. The selloff spread to US memory/semis with SOX -7.9% that day, amplified by -$16bn/1% levered ETF short-gamma structure. Korean regulator admitted it approved leveraged chip ETFs 'too hastily.' SK Hynix separately announced plans for a $29.4B US ADR listing on Nasdaq (targeting July 10) to fund HBM capacity expansion.

bullets.title: Geopolitical: Iran Conflict Easing, Oil Plunges; Hormuz Reopens but Risk Remains Asymmetric
bullets.body: Oil fell ~9% on the week as Persian Gulf crude exports recovered to ~75% of pre-war levels and the US-Iran MOU allowed dollar-denominated oil trade for the first time in 40+ years. WTI broke below $70/bbl. JPM lowered its Brent forecast to $86 3Q26, $80 4Q26, $64 avg 2027. However, a second wave of US military strikes on Iran occurred over the weekend and the ceasefire remains 'tenuous'—Iran struck a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz Saturday. A resumption of conflict would re-spike oil and recessionary tail risk remains non-trivial.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Positioning at Extreme: Tech Hardware >4z, Semis >3z—Prior Peaks Marked Reversals
bullets.body: GS Prime data: Global Semis HF positioning at +3z on 6-month z-score; Tech Hardware even more extreme at >4z (prior peaks near +2z tended to mark highs). Mag7 net exposure at 3-year lows after 5 straight weeks of net selling. Goldman estimated $30B of US equity selling at month/quarter-end (89th percentile) while JPM modeled ~$165B of equity selling/bond buying. Combined levered ETF AUM at ~$200B with $400B in net exposure and trading volumes 50% above H1 2025 pace.

bullets.title: AI Open-Source/China Competition Cited as Structural Headwind to Frontier Model Economics
bullets.body: China's Z.ai GLM 5.2 matched Anthropic Claude performance at 1/5th the cost; DeepSeek and Moonshot also gaining enterprise share. Google lost multiple senior DeepMind researchers to Anthropic and OpenAI (including Nobel laureate AlphaFold creator John Jumper). MSFT CEO Nadella signaled shift away from frontier model dependence toward model choice and lower-cost inference. OpenAI delayed IPO to 2027 and Trump admin asked OpenAI to stagger GPT-5.6 release. 22V expects US restrictions on Chinese AI models post-2026 with retaliation via rare earth controls.

bullets.title: Consumer Spending Resilient Despite Weak Sentiment: Redbook +10% YoY, Real PCE +2.1%
bullets.body: Johnson Redbook same-store sales hit 10% YoY—fastest since post-COVID reopening. Real consumer spending rose 2.1% YoY in May despite UMich sentiment at multi-decade lows (49.5 in June). PSC Daily Consumer Confidence tracks spending far more accurately than UMich: their proprietary survey bottomed well above prior crisis troughs and is now climbing. OpenTable reservations at 99.7th percentile YoY. The divergence reflects lower gas prices and wealth-effect support rather than broad demand strength.

bullets.title: Broader Market Rotation: Industrials, Banks, Homebuilders, Small Caps Outperforming
bullets.body: Russell 2000 outperformed S&P 500 by ~1,240bps YTD—largest small-cap margin since 2003. Healthcare (+6%), Staples (+3%), Utilities (+4.5%), and REITs (+4%) led as defensive rotation occurred. Finance sector dominated 52-week high lists (92 highs vs 11 lows). Industrials consensus EPS revised sharply higher YTD as real economy justifies higher expectations and investment narrative broadens beyond AI. Regional banks (KRE) outperforming on loan growth, robust credit quality, and NIM expansion in higher-for-longer environment; DFAST stress tests showed smallest CET1 drawdown in 7 years (1.6%).

bullets.title: Info Tech/Comm Svcs Net Selling: Largest in 10+ Years Per GS Prime
bullets.body: GS Prime reported Info Tech and Comm Svcs combined net selling as the largest in over 10 years for the week. Global equities saw largest percentage net selling in 3 months (-2.9 SDs) driven by short and long sales 1.7:1. Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 7.2 pts to 199.2% (1-year low). Retail, by contrast, aggressively bought dips—estimated $43B of equity demand Mon-Thu (100th percentile), with $23B in single stocks and $20B via ETFs. MU was the #1 retail buy.

bullets.title: AI Power Demand: Grid Capacity Near Zero by 2027; BYOG and Nuclear Gaining as Speed-to-Power Solutions
bullets.body: US datacenter headroom approaching zero by 2027. EPC capacity severely constrained—GE Vernova cannot book 2029 slots without construction commitments. Speed-to-power is shifting investment toward distributed/behind-the-meter solutions: Chevron-MSFT 20-year BTM deal, Tesla-RUN 16GW virtual power plant framework, and Walmart signing 30-year nuclear PPA with Constellation at Dresden. DOE committed $17.5B in loans for 10 Westinghouse AP1000 reactors. Virginia approved $0.011/kWh data center electricity tax effective July 2026.

bullets.title: Samsung Announces ~W1,000tr (~$648B) AI/Semiconductor Investment Plan
bullets.body: Samsung Group expected to announce a decade-long ~W1,000tr investment on June 29 centered on semiconductors and AI: ~W300tr for 4-5 fabs in Gwangju, W360tr for 6 fabs at Yongin (accelerated from 2048E to 2034E), >W350tr for AI data centers in Asan, and >W56tr for packaging in Chungcheong. SK Hynix separately filed for a $29.4B US ADR listing. Citi and JPM view Samsung's mega-capex as positive for semiconductor equipment makers (AMAT, LRCX, ASML).

bullets.title: June Flash PMIs Strong: Manufacturing 4-Year High, Capex Nowcaster at 10.2% Annualized
bullets.body: US S&P Manufacturing PMI rose to 55.7 in June (4-year high); new orders at 57.5%, future output at 70.1%—strongest reading since February. Services PMI at 51.3% with Services best in 4 months. JPM global capex nowcaster at 10.2% annualized for 2Q26 (up from 6.8% in 1Q), with DM at 9.8% and EM at 19.0%. Duke/Atlanta Fed CFO survey shows revenue expectations up ~50bp since Q1, employment and capex intentions higher. Supply chain delivery times worst since mid-2022.

bullets.title: PCE PCE Methodology Change Coming Sept 30: Could Knock ~20bp Off Core PCE
bullets.body: BEA previewed annual national accounts update: software deflator shifting from CPI-only to CPI-PPI composite, potentially lowering core PCE y/y by up to 20bp if applied retroactively. Legal services shifting to PPI-based composite (mild upside offsetting some software effect). Portfolio management methodology also forthcoming with equity-market-linked adjustment. Morgan Stanley flags this as a potential near-term dove catalyst for Fed expectations if the September revision is significant.

bullets.title: Hedge Fund Gross Leverage Peaked at Unusual Levels; CTA/Risk Parity De-grossing Underway
bullets.body: Hedge fund gross leverage hit unusual peaks in May (+22% vs 6% average) and June (+18% vs 10% average); historically large post-expiry declines of ~5% have followed such peak-leverage conditions. CTAs are significantly long but near deleveraging triggers after the week's pullback. Risk parity funds retreating from highest leverage levels in over a decade. JPM estimated $30B of US equity selling at month-end (89th percentile). Retail options buying peaked around June 5 at ~14M contracts—matching prior peaks in Oct 2025 and Nov 2021 that preceded multi-month tech corrections.

bullets.title: 2Q26 Corporate Earnings: S&P Expected +22% YoY, Highest Since 2021—Heavily Concentrated
bullets.body: S&P 500 EPS expected to grow 22% YoY in Q2—highest estimate since 2021—but median stock only +9%; AI infrastructure expected to contribute ~60% of aggregate S&P growth. MU and NVDA alone account for >40%. Retail sector beat rate was 85.3% in 1Q26 vs 78.9% for S&P 1500. Capital markets activity strong: 2Q26 equity issuance tracking +110% YoY, IPOs up ~5x, announced M&A +60% YoY; global M&A on track for $4T in 2026.
